title: The Growth Kinetic and Ultra High Hardness of CoCrFeNiTi High–Entropy Alloy by Mechanical Alloying and Spark Plasma Sintering

recollection.starting_material: Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, Ti elemental powders (guess)
recollection.intervention: Mechanical alloying followed by Spark Plasma Sintering (guess)
recollection.structure: Single-phase FCC or BCC solid solution with ultra-high hardness (guess)
recollection.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening and grain refinement via severe plastic deformation and rapid sintering (guess)
recollection.results: Hardness values exceeding 1000 HV and improved wear resistance compared to conventional alloys (guess)

score.note: The intervention only repeats what is stated in the title and omits milling and SPS conditions. The proposed single-phase structure is incorrect; the reported alloy had a mixed 83% FCC/17% BCC nanocrystalline structure. The strengthening explanation correctly identifies solid-solution strengthening and grain refinement from mechanical alloying. The claimed >1000 HV hardness is far from the actual 675 HV, and the recalled wear result is unsupported.
